key_insight: OKA-CT improves CT vision-language pretraining by organizing report knowledge around anatomical structures, letting the model learn disease evidence at the organ level instead of only matching whole scans to whole reports.
clinical_relevance: This could make automated CT understanding more sensitive to where abnormalities are located, which may help downstream tasks like abnormality detection and report-image alignment.
method: Parses free-text radiology reports into organ-conditioned hierarchical knowledge with LLM-assisted structuring
Uses organ-level supervision to ground CT visual features in anatomy during stage 1
Uses organ-specific contrastive learning with soft semantic positives, plus a lightweight global query branch, during stage 2
evidence_signal: On CT-RATE and RAD-ChestCT, the model achieved zero-shot abnormality diagnosis AUROCs of 84.9 and 72.2, with retrieval and patch-occlusion results indicating better anatomical alignment.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable report parsing and semantic structuring, so performance may be sensitive to noisy reports, domain shift, or errors in the organ-level knowledge extraction pipeline.
paper_title: Learning Anatomy-Grounded CT Vision-Language Representations with Organ-Hierarchical Report Knowledge
